extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; educated general readers interested in literary theory and the idea of the 'Great Man' (heroes, poets, reformers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes Carlyle's evaluative criteria for 'Hero-Poets' and 'Hero-Priests' (e.g., Shakespeare, Dante, Luther) — the qualities by which such figures and their works are judged as great or effective. Useful for literary criticism and creative-writing concerned with heroic figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeing / The 'seeing eye' (intellect as insight)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The seeing eye... that discloses the inner harmony of things; what Nature meant, what musical idea Nature has wrapped up in these often rough embodiments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Carlyle's primary criterion: the poet must 'see' the inmost heart and generic secret of things so clearly that the appropriate words and forms follow. Examples/explanations: 'To the Poet... See. If you cannot do that, it is of no use to keep stringing rhymes together.' Practical test: can the author find true beginnings, sequences and endings; 'Fiat lux' — make order out of chaos. Anti-pattern: mere rhyming, 'jingling sensibilities.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Superiority of Intellect (unity of faculties)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'If called to define Shakspeare's faculty, I should say superiority of Intellect' — intellect understood as an indivisible, superior power that integrates imagination, fancy, understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carlyle emphasizes an integrated intellectual power that produces calm depth, deliberate illumination, and a capacity to construct and 'discern' the fit form from disorderly material. Comparison: Bacon's Novum Organum is 'of a quite secondary order.' Use as criterion: evaluate breadth, calmness, and constructing power of mind manifested in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral Nature / Virtue as precondition of true knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Without morality, intellect were impossible for him; a thoroughly immoral man could not know anything at all!... To know a thing... a man must first love the thing, sympathize with it: that is, be virtuously related to it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True insight requires moral qualities — justice, courage, disinterestedness — because knowledge depends on sympathetic, 'virtuous' relation to the object. Anti-pattern: selfish, cynical 'Fox' knowledge (knowing 'where the geese lodge') — practical but shallow. Evaluate a writer's ethics and sympathy as part of aesthetic judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconsciousness / Naturalness (art not artifice)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Shakspeare's Art is not Artifice; the noblest worth of it is not there by plan or precontrivance. It grows up from the deeps of Nature... an unconscious intellect.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that grow organically from the author's inner nature are higher than contrived, calculated art. Indicators: sense of inevitability, fresh meanings discovered by later generations, 'symmetry grounded on Nature's own laws.' Anti-pattern: over-calculation, deliberate contrivance that hides lack of native force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality and Sincerity (veracity and perennial reach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspeare 'reaches deep down... to the universal and perennial' and is 'sincere' like Homer or Aeschylus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work's ability to speak to human beings across times and cultures — its 'veracity' — marks greatness. Evaluate whether characters, feelings, and truths feel broadly human (not merely topical). Comparison examples: Homer, Aeschylus, Dante.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait-painting / Complete delineation of character
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is in... delineating of men and things, especially of men, that Shakspeare is great... sets them all forth to us in their round completeness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how fully and generically the writer renders characters' inner mechanisms and 'inward mechanism' (Goethe quote). Examples: Falstaff, Othello, Juliet, Coriolanus. Anti-pattern: flat, caricatural figures lacking inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apt Language Arising from Sight
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The word that will describe the thing, follows of itself from such clear intense sight of the thing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriateness and inevitability of diction: language feels compelled by vision rather than decorative. Test: whether phrasing/provocation seems the natural expression of an apprehended reality rather than a clever surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genial Laughter / Sympathetic Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspeare's 'genuine overflowing love of laughter' that 'never' laughs at misery or poverty; 'Laughter means sympathy; good laughter is not "the crackling of thorns under the pot."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate humor for its sympathy and humanity rather than derision. Examples: Dogberry and Verges make us laugh yet love them. Anti-pattern: mean-spirited, superior, mocking laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation to Materials and Conditions (craft & fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He discerns... what his materials are, what his own force and its relation to them is... The built house seems all so fit... the very perfection of the house... hides the builder's merit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great artists understand constraints and produce work suited to their materials and circumstances (e.g., Shakespeare writing for the Globe). Assess how well form, scale, and medium fit the author's aim. Recognize 'disjecta membra' — works are often fragmentary products of circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance / Lastingness over worldly effect
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is not by what is called their effect on the world... that a man and his work are measured.' Also: Dante 'burns as a pure star... he may long survive Mahomet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value long-term nobility, clarity and depth over immediate mass influence or political/temporal success. Test: whether the work continues to yield meaning beyond contemporary fame or power. Anti-pattern: loud, immediate public success that is 'a loud-sounding inanity and futility'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony with Nature / Organic Symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: 'With a symmetry grounded on Nature's own laws, conformable to all Truth whatsoever.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge works for a natural, organic order that feels consonant with broader truths and laws rather than arbitrary arrangements. Indicators: sense of inevitability, growth from roots; prophetic resonance with later ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to Make Order from Chaos (structural mastery)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Which circumstance is vital and shall stand prominent; which unessential, fit to be suppressed; where is the true beginning, the true sequence and ending?... Fiat lux, Let there be light; and out of chaos make a world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mastery of structure: selection, suppression of unessential, narrative architecture. Does the writer shape disorderly raw material into a coherent world? Anti-pattern: inability to discern fit structure; scattershot composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity / Justice Toward Objects (level mirror)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspeare is 'a perfectly level mirror... a man justly related to all things and men, a good man.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author presents things fairly and without distortion of personal bias — the capacity to 'take in all kinds of men' with justice and love. Anti-pattern: skewed, biased, or monstrously distorted portrayals reflecting personal deformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Necessity of Individual Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Absolutely without originality there is no man. No man whatever believes, or can believe, exactly what his grandfather believed: he enlarges somewhat, by fresh discovery.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the work's originality and the author's capacity to enlarge or revise received thought. Originality is a necessary condition for meaningful contribution; anti-pattern: mere repetition of inherited forms without enlargement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitivity / account for historical and material constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No man works save under conditions... The sculptor cannot set his own free Thought before us; but his Thought as he could translate it into the stone that was given, with the tools that were given.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging, consider the social, material, and institutional constraints shaping the work (e.g., Shakespeare writing for the Globe; Dante as product of medieval religion). Use context to temper expectations and explain 'disjecta membra.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero as Priest / Spiritual leadership and vocation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The Priest... presides over the worship of the people; is the Uniter of them with the Unseen Holy... He is the spiritual Captain of the people.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reformers and religious figures, evaluate their capacity to function as spiritual leaders: interpret unseen meanings, unite people toward higher ends, and guide daily life. Examples treated: Luther, Knox; the Priest-figure appears as a milder, practical Prophet. Anti-pattern: religious function reduced to political noise or intolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reformer-as-Battling-Priest (capacity for upheaval)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The warfaring and battling Priest; who led his people... to faithful valorous conflict, in times all violent, dismembered: a more perilous service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing reformers or 'heroic' leaders, measure their ability to detect obstructions and to lead forceful, morally grounded change when necessary. This includes courage to overturn ossified systems (Dante's Catholicism torn by Luther). Anti-pattern: inability to act when practice has become dishonest or decayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nation-Voice / Ability to articulate national spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing 'an articulate voice; that it produce a man who will speak forth melodiously what the heart of it means!' — e.g., Dante for Italy, Shakespeare as an English 'King' uniting Englishmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a creative figure furnishes a language or symbolic center that unites dispersed members of a culture or diaspora across time and space. Practical utility: cultural cohesion beyond administrative power (contrast to empires and armies).
